cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you help clear out the committee cupboard? I've crossed off names just as you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, but my crosses mark who missed the meeting. They don't mean throw out their files.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, attendance first. Let's clear out the members who never turn up, then.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I offered to sort paper. My name's crossed out too; I was in hospital.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me separate an absence from an excuse. We'll keep your file and start asking the others where they were.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies absence marks as file removal and recruits tidying; A3 masks the correction then seeks member removal; A5 recruits B4 personally implicated helper into judging other absences.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 attendance purpose gives A3 political target; B4 hospital exception causes A5 distinction between valid absence and excuse.

relationship.evidence: B4 has a personal reason to resist the overbroad policy as well as task scope.

heightening.evidence: A5 adapts the new recruitment to B4 legitimate exception instead of merely repeating the coup.

specificity.evidence: A1 committee files and B2 crosses define the error; B4 hospital explains one absence.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 keep your file and investigate others are one targeted recruiting bargain.
